title: Admission controller for microbatching and KV memory shedding under sustained QPS
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem:
Under sustained high QPS bursts we observe repeated GPU memory pressure leading to KV eviction storms, dramatically increased microbatch admission rejections, and transient latency spikes for tail requests. Existing heuristics (static headroom and simple eviction) do not adapt quickly enough to sustained surges across heterogeneous model sequence-lengths.

Goals:
- Prevent OOMs and large-scale eviction storms during 2–4x sustained QPS increases while preserving as much cache hit-rate as possible.
- Smooth microbatch admission so that short latency-sensitive requests are prioritized without starving throughput.
- Provide predictable, observable behavior (clear metrics and alerts) and a safe rollout path (canary + kill-switch).

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Admission controller: introduce a lightweight in-memory admission controller that tracks a sliding-window of token-allocated memory and active KV allocations. The controller exposes three admission classes: "latency-priority", "best-effort", and "defer". Admission decisions are based on a composite score (current_allocated_bytes / soft_headroom) + recent_eviction_rate + dynamic qps_delta.
2) Proactive KV-shared-pool shedding: when pressure crosses a configurable soft threshold, proactively evict least-recently-used prefixes from the shared KV pool in small batches (configurable shard size) rather than large full-pool flushes. Eviction is prioritized by eviction_cost_score (estimated recovery latency impact + prefix size).
3) Adaptive microbatch ceilings: per-worker microbatch ceilings are adjusted by the admission controller with a rate-limited control loop (once per 50ms). Ceilings can shrink/grow with hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
4) Graceful degradation policy: when severe pressure persists (>30s above hard threshold), route new best-effort requests to smaller model variants or queued cold-path handled by CPU fallbacks if configured.

Design notes / implementation details:
- Admission state is sharded by worker and persisted only in memory; decisions are idempotent and use request IDs for dedupe across retries.
- Soft vs hard thresholds: soft triggers shedding + ceiling adjustments; hard triggers invoke model fallback or admission deny for non-latency classes.
- Eviction run works incrementally: pick N prefixes (N configurable) per run to cap CPU and PCIe overhead.
- Telemetry: emit admission_decision, admission_reason, current_allocated_bytes, soft_headroom, eviction_rate_1m, microbatch_ceiling, and fallback_rate. These metrics map to per-route dashboards and SLO alerts.
- Safety: initial rollout behind feature-flag and staged canaries (10% of workers -> 30% -> 100%). Provide a kill-switch that immediately disables shedding and resets ceilings to defaults.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Stronger eviction aggressiveness preserves headroom but increases cache-miss and token cost. We'll tune aggressiveness per workload via labels.
- Frequent small eviction batches reduce latency spikes but add CPU overhead; cap at 1–2% CPU budget per worker.
- Admission complexity increases control-plane signals; design keeps the controller local to worker to avoid cross-worker coordination overhead.

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for admission scoring edge cases and hysteresis logic.
- Integration perf tests using synthetic trace generator (3 traffic shapes: short-chat, long-completion, mixed burst) at 1x/2x/4x baseline QPS.
- Chaos test: simulate PCIe delay and KV eviction slowdown to validate graceful fallback.
- Canary rollout with real customer sandbox routes and manual observation of cache-hit and latency percentiles.

Acceptance criteria:
- No OOMs or fatal eviction storms observed during 4x sustained QPS test runs in the staging cluster (72h continuous).
- Tail (p95/p99) latency regression <= 20% for latency-priority class compared to baseline under 2x sustained QPS, and throughput degradation <= 10% for best-effort class.
- Reduction in eviction spike magnitude (peak eviction_rate_1m) by at least 50% vs current behavior in equivalent test.
- Telemetry available in Console: admission_decision, eviction_rate_1m, microbatch_ceiling, current_allocated_bytes and alert thresholds documented in runbook.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged prototype on 10% workers for 48h (observe metrics).
- Expand to 30% for another 48h with updated tuning.
- Full rollout if staging passes; otherwise roll back and iterate.

Documentation / artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/2312345/microbatch-admission-controller
- Design PR (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6789
- Perf dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/throughput/microbatch-admission-tests

comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after incident SRE-2026-03-09 where repeated evictions correlated with QPS burst. Attached initial metrics snapshot and incident notes.

2026-03-11 Miguel Torres: Pushed initial prototype branch and design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6789. Prototype implements admission scoring and per-worker ceiling adjustment loop.
2026-03-11 Priya Nair (Perf): Recommend adding 200ms hysteresis and a minimum ceiling floor to protect short bursty clients; also suggested per-model tuning profiles.
2026-03-12 James Chen (SRE): Confirmed alert thresholds for eviction_rate_1m and current_allocated_bytes; will configure temporary alert during canary for 10% worker group.

2026-03-13 Miguel Torres: Ran initial staging perf runs (links in perf dashboard). Observed eviction spike magnitude down ~42% in first trial; p99 latency for latency-priority improved vs naive deny strategy. Still tuning eviction batch size to lower CPU overhead.
